root.before: Bare sxr lists every Claude session in the exact current directory, newest first. @N handles refer to the filtered scope. Root options are merged by most session commands.
root.default_before: Claude. Exact cwd. Unlimited sessions. Text table.
root.problem: Root options are silently ignored by init, skills and parts of index/serve. Root help is long. Provider defaults differ from find.
root.after: Keep bare listing and current provider defaults. Share one option contract across entry paths. Reject irrelevant root options. State the selected provider and scope in help and notices.
root.default_after: Same listing defaults. No silently ignored options.
root.compatibility: Rejecting previously ignored options can expose existing script mistakes. Preserve documented list behavior.
root.acceptance: Compare options before/after each compatible command. Unsupported options fail with a targeted explanation. Empty lists still exit 0.

list.before: Lists scoped sessions with metadata and temporary @N handles. Text and JSON list sessions. Empty scope exits 0.
list.default_before: Claude. Exact cwd. All sessions. Newest start first.
list.problem: No handle or exact follow-up command in JSON. Timestamp formatting replaces offsets with Z without converting. Ordering compares timestamp strings.
list.after: Keep list and empty-result behavior. Normalize instants before sorting/formatting. Include handle, scope and exact file follow-up in structured metadata.
list.default_after: Same selection and limits. Correct UTC timestamps.
list.compatibility: Additional JSON fields are additive. Corrected chronology can change @N numbering for offset-bearing records.
list.acceptance: Equivalent offset timestamps sort by instant. Copy a JSON follow-up after scope changes and read the same file.

show.before: Shows text, tool calls and turn context from the newest selected session. Fits whole text under a 40000-character threshold, otherwise trims. --full and zooms print whole text. Session ranges silently use only the first session.
show.default_before: Newest session. Skeleton. Unlimited selected events. Budget 40000. Line cap 200.
show.problem: Filters override each other by branch order. Range selectors discard sessions. --tools means tool results even though tool calls already appear.
show.after: Honor every session in a range with source identity. Compose filters and windows in a documented order. Retain skeleton/full behavior. Add --tool-results as the clear name for --tools.
show.default_after: Same skeleton. Explicit filters narrow full output.
show.compatibility: Combined flags will select differently. Keep --tools as an alias. A range will produce more output as requested.
show.acceptance: --full --errors prints only errors without trimming. --type plus --around intersects. A two-session range includes both source identities.

prompts.before: Selects human-labelled user records, falling back to legacy user text when provenance is absent. All selected rows are printed by default, but long text is trimmed above the budget. --all adds injected context and tool results.
prompts.default_before: Newest session. All human-selected rows. Budget 40000. Line cap 200.
prompts.problem: A simple request for human prompts requires a trimming workaround. --all changes what counts as a prompt. Session ranges silently read the first session.
prompts.after: Print complete human prompts by default. --all lifts presentation limits while retaining human selection. --include-context explicitly includes other user-role records and labels their provenance. Honor ranges.
prompts.default_after: All complete human prompts. No implicit budget or line trimming.
prompts.compatibility: --all changes meaning and needs a migration note to --include-context. Large outputs become intentional. Preserve explicit --budget for compact views.
prompts.acceptance: Plain prompts contains every human prompt verbatim under SXR_BUDGET=1. --all never adds injected records. --include-context is explicit. Both providers and legacy provenance are covered.

errors.before: Prints records with error properties across selected sessions, deduplicated by tool call ID or record. Text always trims the middle to 200+120 characters. JSON emits complete distinct source records.
errors.default_before: Newest session. All errors. Trimmed text.
errors.problem: Rows from multiple sessions have only local sequence numbers. Whole error text requires another command or JSON.
errors.after: Include source session/file coordinates on each result. Print complete error text by default and offer --compact for summaries. Keep recorded error properties as the selection rule.
errors.default_after: All complete error records with source identity.
errors.compatibility: Text layout and volume change. Raw JSON remains available and unmodified.
errors.acceptance: Two errors at the same sequence in different sessions stay distinguishable. Long error endings and middles survive default output. Limits remain global.

tools.before: Counts tool calls and failures by tool in the first selected session. Text -n counts tool rows. JSON always emits one complete aggregate. Skill inputs appear in an uncapped text footer.
tools.problem: A range loses all but the first session. --limit measures tool rows only in text. Skill input output escapes the limit.
tools.after: Honor ranges with one identified summary per session. Apply --limit consistently to tool entries in either format. Render Skill input detail as bounded data or explicit detail output.
tools.default_after: All tool types per selected session.
tools.compatibility: Capped JSON aggregates need explicit totals/omitted metadata. Document the change before altering existing complete-object behavior.
tools.acceptance: Both sessions appear. Text/JSON include the same tool keys under -n. Skill detail cannot grow unnoticed outside the requested cap.

stats.before: Prints session properties and counts. Text -n limits field/value rows globally. JSON -n limits whole session objects. Some JSON counts and sizes are human-formatted strings.
stats.problem: The same limit returns one property in text and an entire session in JSON. Numeric fields and timestamps are inconsistent for agents.
stats.after: Make --limit count complete session summaries in both formats. Keep JSON counts/sizes numeric and emit accurate UTC timestamps. Group text fields under an explicit session identity.
stats.default_after: Complete summaries for all selected sessions.
stats.compatibility: Changes text limit units and selected JSON field types. Version or document the structured schema migration.
stats.acceptance: -n 1 means one complete session in either format. Tokens and size_bytes are numeric. Offset timestamps preserve the instant.

path.before: Prints distinct provider session file paths for selected references, with main file first. JSON emits type=path objects. Limits count paths.
path.default_before: Newest session. All paths returned by provider.session_paths.
path.problem: The exact file set is implicit and differs from clean's physical duplicate/child expansion. Singular command accepts multiple files but JSON lacks owning session identity.
path.after: Keep the name and one-path-per-line output. Document physical file expansion and align it with the scope used by audit/clean. Add source session/provider fields in JSON.
path.default_after: Explicitly documented file scope. Unlimited paths.
path.compatibility: JSON fields are additive. Any file-scope change must be verified against existing child/copy behavior.
path.acceptance: Every reported path belongs to the selected scope. File deduplication and -n remain deterministic. --file yields only that file.

grep.before: Searches normalized event text with smart-case regex across all scoped sessions. -c counts events by session. -l prints IDs. Default match rows are flattened to 200 characters with a 40000-character total output budget.
grep.default_before: Claude. All sessions in exact cwd. Smart-case regex. No row cap. Display budget 40000.
grep.problem: -n 0 also disables the budget but still leaves per-match trimming. JSON can duplicate a physical record and -l --json prints plain IDs. -C limits blocks rather than physical lines.
grep.after: Keep search semantics. Make count and text limits independent and explicit. Add --full for complete matched text and --all for uncapped output. Rename zero-count inclusion to --include-zero. Enforce JSON and deduplication contracts.
grep.default_after: Bounded search summaries. Clear recovery to complete matches.
grep.compatibility: --all and -n 0 changes need migration notes. Preserve regex/smart-case behavior and exact counts.
grep.acceptance: -l --json is valid structured output. A source record is emitted once in raw JSON. --all restores all complete matches. Count totals remain independent of display caps.

cmds.before: Lists every parsed tool call, including non-shell tools, with paired outcome. No selector uses the newest session, except a nonempty --grep searches the entire scope. Text commands are trimmed at SXR_LINE_LIMIT (200).
cmds.default_before: Newest session. All tool calls. Text cap 200 per command.
cmds.problem: Filtering changes session scope. The name suggests shell commands but Read and other tools appear. JSON returns raw calls without normalized paired outcomes and can repeat physical records.
cmds.after: Keep cmds as the compatibility name and describe it as recorded tool calls and shell commands. Show complete call text by default. Add --all-sessions for explicit scope and --events-json for one call with its outcome and source coordinates.
cmds.default_after: Newest session regardless of --grep. Whole call text.
cmds.compatibility: Implicit all-session --grep behavior must be migrated to --all-sessions. Preserve all-tool coverage and cmds spelling.
cmds.acceptance: Adding a filter does not change scope. Structured calls retain separate tool blocks and paired outcomes without duplicate raw records.

init.before: Bare init prints the primer. --write installs or replaces a marked block. --check checks marker version only. Default target is nearest AGENTS.md, with --global using a separate fallback chain.
init.problem: A modified block stamped with the current version passes --check. Root --json and scope options may be accepted but ignored. Global target selection is not obvious.
init.after: Keep print/write/check operations. Compare installed block content as well as version. Expose resolved target in diagnostics and help. Reject irrelevant inherited options.
init.default_after: Print only. Explicit --write required for changes.
init.compatibility: --check becomes stricter. Preserve prose outside primer markers and idempotent writes.
init.acceptance: A modified current-version block fails --check. Existing outside text remains byte-identical after --write. Invalid destinations fail with exit 2.

index.before: Builds/refreshes the substring candidate index for selected Claude sessions by default. --clear removes the shared search database. Ranked find preparation is separately exposed through find --index.
index.default_before: Refresh substring index for Claude sessions in cwd.
index.problem: Two indexing commands prepare different structures in the same cache. Root --json/-n are ignored. --clear bypasses provider/scope validation.
index.after: Make index refresh both substring and ranked session search structures in the explicitly selected scope. Retain find --index as a compatible entry with its documented scope defaults. Reject meaningless limit/clear scope combinations.
index.default_after: Refresh all session-search structures for selected scope.
index.compatibility: Index work may take longer. Preserve cache location and clear behavior. Add structured operation output before accepting --json.
index.acceptance: A prepared scope supports warm grep and find. --clear reports its actual cache extent. Root and command JSON behavior agree.

find.before: Ranks sessions by case-insensitive word/phrase clues across both providers, Claude children and present Codex archives. Requires every clue by default. Refreshes its index and excludes the invoking Codex session when identified.
find.default_before: Exact cwd. Both providers. Children/archives included. Five ranked sessions, or all paths with --paths.
find.problem: Fast and Typer parsers have different help/abbreviation behavior. Typer --claude help incorrectly calls Claude the default. Quoting requirements and no-op inclusion flags add friction.
find.after: Keep retrieval semantics and bounded evidence. Derive both parser entry paths from one command contract, accept several clue arguments, accurately describe defaults, and add explicit exclusion counterparts for children/archives.
find.default_after: Same scope, ranking, current-session exclusion and five-result cap.
find.compatibility: Extra clue positionals are additive. Reject abbreviated long flags consistently. Preserve exact --file follow-ups and incomplete-search exit 2.
find.acceptance: Flags before/after find produce matching results, help and validation. Quoted phrase behavior remains intact. Every hit retains source-backed evidence.

skills.before: Discovers SKILL.md paths on first use or --index, groups identical contents, and reuses a saved map. Searches path/name clues. Uncached default discovery covers HOME plus configured roots outside it.
skills.default_before: Saved discovery map. 20 content groups in table/JSON. All groups with --paths.
skills.problem: Root --json/-n are ignored. --paths/--aliases projection differs in JSON. --root remembers scope only with --index. Several maintenance flags silently ignore output options.
skills.after: Preserve path lookup and content grouping. Make inherited applicable flags work, document discovery/remembered roots, validate maintenance combinations, and align path projection in text/JSON.
skills.default_after: Same discovery roots and lookup limits. Consistent option placement.
skills.compatibility: Fixes formerly ignored root flags. Path-only JSON changes shape and needs a schema note. Keep existing grouping/copy semantics.
skills.acceptance: Root/local JSON and limits agree. --paths --aliases --json returns the same paths as text. Scoped lookups never alter remembered default roots.

secrets.before: Without a subcommand audits all scoped session references for certain/probable secrets and prints masked salted fingerprints. An optional session selector is redirected to hidden audit. --candidates adds entropy candidates.
secrets.default_before: Claude. Entire exact-cwd scope. Certain/probable only. Unlimited masked rows.
secrets.problem: Auditing scans ref.path, while clean expands copies and children. Reserved action names collide with session names. The suggested raw show command can expose the secret and loses scope.
secrets.after: Use the same explicit physical-file scope for audit, path and clean. Keep masking and current finding criteria. Expose audit as a documented action and give exact masked follow-ups instead of raw secret-bearing zooms.
secrets.default_after: Same masked audit with explicitly defined child/copy scope.
secrets.compatibility: Keep shorthand secrets SESSION and bare audit. Align scope carefully before changing file selection.
secrets.acceptance: Audit and clean preview inspect the same selected physical files. Text/JSON never contain secret values. Duplicate paths are counted once.

secrets audit.before: Hidden explicit alias for the default masked secret audit. Accepts a session selector plus audit and scope flags.
secrets audit.default_before: Same as bare secrets. All sessions in scope.
secrets audit.problem: The clearer action name exists but is hidden from help. Parent --candidates propagation is implicit.
secrets audit.after: Document audit as a first-class action while preserving bare secrets and secrets SESSION. Show audit-only flags on the audit surface.
secrets audit.compatibility: Help visibility is additive. Preserve the existing shortcut grammar.
secrets audit.acceptance: Help lists audit and clean. Shared flags and --candidates work consistently at supported group levels.

secrets clean.before: Previews certain/probable replacements across selected references plus their physical copies and Claude children. --apply rewrites atomically, skipping live/changed files, and clears caches. -n caps report rows only.
secrets clean.default_before: Dry run. All scoped references and expanded physical files. Unlimited report rows.
secrets clean.problem: Preview/apply follow-up drops the selected scope. Parent --candidates is accepted but ignored. A live-file skip is not an incomplete-operation exit. Physical scope differs from audit.
secrets clean.after: Keep explicit --apply, atomic replacement and report-only limits. Print an exact apply command preserving every selector. Align physical scope with audit and return machine-readable skipped/failed/changed counts.
secrets clean.compatibility: Do not broaden writes as part of UX changes. Define skipped-live reporting without changing its existing exit semantics until documented.
secrets clean.acceptance: Copying the preview follow-up touches only the previewed scope. -n never reduces validation or hides the summary of changed/skipped files. Candidate findings remain excluded.

serve.before: Manages the optional local worker. Default action is status, with stop available. Direct argparse also accepts hidden --foreground PATH and --idle SECONDS. Root-prefixed Typer wrapper only accepts action.
serve.default_before: status. Internal foreground idle timeout 300 seconds.
serve.problem: Moving a root flag changes accepted flags/help. Internal flags have combinations that silently override or ignore action. --idle accepts non-finite floats.
serve.after: Use one parser contract. Keep status/stop and private launcher controls separate in help and validation. Reject incompatible or non-finite internal arguments.
serve.default_after: Same worker lifecycle and idle timeout.
serve.compatibility: Preserve native launcher's hidden arguments. Do not start/stop a real worker during report generation.
serve.acceptance: Both entry paths validate identically. Idle must be finite and positive. Internal foreground launch remains compatible with the bundle.
